I've been looking at the proposed tax policies of the Presidential candidates and trying to figure out which one I think will be the most effective and fair. I've also been reading a lot and watching documentaries on issues with the tax system. Currently I'm watching "We're Not Broke", which is about large multinational corporations who aren't paying their "fair share" of taxes due to offshore tax havens and complex accounting practices, although it all within the legal bounds of the US tax code. This documentary is very biased toward higher taxes and higher govenrment spending; however, it's showing that the real problem is the US corporate tax rate, which is 35% and currently the highest in the world. Corporations are refusing to pay that outragous rate and are claiming their revenue in other countries with more reasonable tax rates...and nobody can really, logically blame them.

Enactng a flat rate income tax, or better yet, a flat rate consumption tax such as the FairTax, would make the US a tax haven and corporations would WANT to base their operations here, employ American workers, and contribute tax revenue to OUR country instead of other countries. It's so logical, so easy to understand...I just can't wrap my head around why people don't support one of these tax policies. The only reason must be that they don't understand the policies. A consumption tax would collect a share from the billions of dollars that are earned in black market activities where our current tax policy doesn't collect a penny, since these people aren't claiming their income on illegal activities. It would put the consumer in control of their tax burden. If you don't want to pay a lot in taxes, don't consume as much...it's really that simple. You would receive a prebate for goods that are requried for life, like food, and the cost of goods would drop due to the removal of the corporate tax; this has been proven historically by the airline industry when it was deregulated and the price of airfare decreased by the amount of the tax that was abolished.

It's just common sense to support a policy such as this, but even if you don't want to go full consumption tax (for whatever reason), a flat income tax is a step in the right direciton. Lowering the corporate tax to 14.5% like Rand Paul wants to do would entice corporations to base their operations here in the US, pay their taxes because the rate is reasonale, and employ American workers, which would create jobs. It's a win-win situation and easily the most logical policy
